description.content: The exact call an LLM agent's purchase() tool makes. Checks the mandate (amount, currency, payee, window, cumulative cap), executes with a deterministic PayPal-Request-Id, journals every step, and answers with a signed receipt — or a signed refusal with the precise reason. Wallet-funded orders stop at PAYER_ACTION_REQUIRED and return the buyer approval redirect (two-phase, human-in-the-loop).

item.name: paypal-tools
item.description: PayPal's official agent tools (@paypal/mcp — 28 tools) re-exposed behind the Carte Blanche wall: every call needs a live signed mandate; create_order / pay_order / create_refund are measured against the mandate first; refusals are signed denials; forwarded calls land in the sealed journal.

item.name: List PayPal's tools available behind the wall

request.name: List PayPal's tools available behind the wall

description.content: The 28 tools of PayPal's official MCP server, each with its class: read (list_/get_/show_/generate_), write (changes PayPal state without moving money), spend (create_order, pay_order, create_refund). Every one requires mandate_id. 503 on mock rails (no PayPal to speak to).

response.name: Mock rails — PayPal's tools need sandbox credentials

item.name: Call one of PayPal's tools through the wall

request.name: Call one of PayPal's tools through the wall

description.content: Forwards PayPal's own tool with PayPal's own arguments — after the wall. Spend tools: create_order is priced from its items (× cost, + tax, + shipping, − discount); pay_order reads the order back (get_order) before the walls run; create_refund needs an explicit amount (a mandate cannot cover "whatever the capture was"). A refusal returns the same signed denial a purchase gets (verifiable at /verify/{id}); PayPal is never called. Forwarded calls are journalled (external_call_authorized → external_call_completed | external_call_failed | external_spend); money is counted against the mandate only when PayPal confirms it moved.

response.name: Forwarded (with PayPal's result and the evidence position) or refused (signed denial)

description.content:
Spending mandates, sealed receipts and dispute-proof audits for AI agents paying with PayPal.

The agent boundary is `POST /api/agent/purchase`: every call is checked against a signed, immutable mandate *before* money moves, executed with a deterministic `PayPal-Request-Id` (a retry can never double-spend), and answered with a signed receipt — or a signed proof of refusal. Every event lands in an append-only SHA-256 chain with signed checkpoints, CT-style Merkle inclusion proofs and RFC 3161 TSA anchoring.

This contract is ready for APIMatic import (developer portal + SDK generation): point it at the raw `openapi.json` served by the live instance.
